title: Inline, internal, and external CSS
learningObjectives: Choose and write maintainable CSS selectors for inline, internal, and external css.

understand.concept: CSS can be added with a style attribute, a style element or an external .css file linked with link. External stylesheets are usually easier to reuse and maintain.
understand.whyItMatters: Good selectors target intended elements and keep styles maintainable.
understand.analogy: Selectors are like finding items in a list by their labels or relationships.
understand.analogyLimit: Selectors are not just labels; the document tree, state and specificity also matter.

explain.narrative: CSS can be added with a style attribute, a style element or an external .css file linked with link. External stylesheets are usually easier to reuse and maintain.

examples.code: Reusable styles
examples.explanation: Change the selector and observe which elements match.
examples.expectedOutput: Matching elements receive the CSS styles.

practise.guidedTask: Change one selector and observe how many elements match.
practise.independentTask: Create a small stylesheet with reusable classes for cards, headings and link states.
hints: Do not remove visible keyboard focus styles.

practice.starterCode: Reusable styles
practice.resetCode: Reusable styles

questions.prompt: Which approach is generally easiest to reuse across pages?
questions.explanation: Identify the selector syntax and matching rule.

questions.prompt: Do overly complex selectors usually improve maintainability?
questions.explanation: Short, clear reusable selectors are easier to maintain.
